text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automatic pager: elevated 5xx + latency detected in eu-central-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Incident ID: RWD-INC-2026-0521. Paging oncall.

alice (sre): I'm taking first look. Metrics show a sudden rise in 502/504 responses originating from our regional auth proxy and observability egress endpoints. p50 latency up ~2x, p95 up ~3x for requests routed to eu-central-1.

bob (oncall): Oncall here. What quick mitigation checks do we have?

alice (sre): Quick checks I ran:
```
# verifying regional reachability
ping -c 5 eu-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com
# many packets lost, TCP handshake resets observed
```
Also checked control-plane logs: token exchange timeouts around the same timeframe. Dedicated pool controller shows worker restart loops for some model workers in az-a.

carla (eng-runtime): Runtime traces show KV-cache refreshes stalling because our obs-exporter and token validation endpoints are timing out. This creates request queueing and causes gateway timeouts upstream.

paul (infra): AWS Health/Status shows a partial network degradation in eu-central-1 affecting several NLB/ELB nodes and intermittent control-plane connectivity in some AZs. Not a full outage but packet loss and increased RTTs.

dev-support: Any active customer tickets?

customer-success: Yes: two Hosted API customers in EU region reporting spike in 5xxs; one Dedicated tenant reporting degraded throughput. CS has notified them we're investigating and offered guidance on cross-region failover.

alice (sre): Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Gradual cross-region routing shift for new Hosted API sessions from eu-central-1 to eu-west-1 (5% -> 25% -> 75%). Keep existing in-flight sessions where possible.
- For Dedicated pools: prevent new allocations in eu-central-1 and start warm up in eu-west-1.
- Reduce egress pressure by disabling non-critical observability exporters in eu-central-1.
- Increase token cache TTL to reduce STS calls temporarily (120s -> 300s) where safe.

carla (eng-runtime): I'll kick off a routing canary to eu-west-1. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/failover -d '{"from":"eu-central-1","to":"eu-west-1","percent":5}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL"
```
Starting canary for 5% at ts 2759994390.

bob (oncall): Watching the canary. If errors drop for canary within 90s, expand to 25%.

paul (infra): Disabling obs-exporter now in eu-central-1 to reduce egress. kubectl scale deployment/obs-exporter --replicas=0 --context=eu-central-1.

incident-bot: Oncall handover scheduled to eve (next shift) in 25m. Incident declared P1-regional.

carla (eng-runtime): Canary results: initial 5% showed error rate reduced to baseline. Expanding to 25% at 2759994455.

later - carla (eng-runtime): 25% stable for 3m. Expanding to 75%.

paul (infra): Dedicated pool controller: marking eu-central-1 as degraded for new allocations, initiating scale-up in eu-west-1 (launched 4 nodes). ETA ~3m for warm workers.

customer-success: Notified impacted customers, offered region migration. One customer accepted immediate migration and requested a hard cutover. Concern about cache stampede.

alice (sre): For hard cutover, advise staged DNS/routing shift and pre-warm model workers. We'll prefer staged to avoid massive concurrent token validation.

bob (oncall): I'll coordinate staged failover for the Dedicated customer if they still want it. Leaving notes for eve for handover.

carla (eng-runtime): Also implemented a temporary safety: model-variant fallback enabled so workers use smaller-memory variants to reduce churn while nodes warm.

alice (sre): After routing changes and disabling obs-exporter, regional 5xxs dropped ~65% and latency improved. Still seeing intermittent 504s for token exchange hitting affected AZs.

paul (infra): Opening AWS support case for NLB/ELB node connectivity in eu-central-1, referencing affected AZs and packet loss traces.

dev-support: Recording affected products: hosted-api (eu-central-1), dedicated-tenant-77 (eu-central-1). Tickets created for each customer.

incident-bot: Incident page created RWD-INC-2026-0521, status: mitigated (partial). Postmortem required.

alice (sre): Next actions:
- Keep cross-region routing in place until AWS confirms region healthy or for 2 hours, whichever is sooner.
- Keep token TTL elevated for 2 hours, then revert if stable.
- Re-enable observability exporters only after confirming egress capacity.
- Compile customer impact summary and runbook updates for the postmortem.

customer-success: Consolidating customer notes and required follow-ups. No escalations as of now.

bob (oncall): Handoff to eve in 20m. Leaving canary and routing state, plus the AWS support ticket number. :thumbsup:

eve (oncall-next): Acknowledged. I'll take over watch and escalate to infra if dedicated migrations are requested.

alice (sre): Good work team. Closing emergency page, incident remains open for monitoring until AWS clears the network flap.

-- end of thread
